<!-- Generated by dev/tools/gen-site-docs (internal/sitedoc). DO NOT EDIT: edit the command metadata / flag declarations / ledgers and re-run the generator. -->

Every `kind=` the read path can emit (150 in all), rendered from the same
`Kinds` declarations that produce each command's `--help`, MCP tool
schema, and reference page. A check cannot emit a kind that is not here:
the contract tests reject an undeclared kind, and a source sweep rejects
one no test happens to exercise.

The severity column is every level the kind can carry, worst first — one
kind often spans two, because the same defect is graver in some shapes
than others. A kind's absence from a run means the check looked and found
nothing (zero nominal state); it never means the check was skipped, which
is reported explicitly.

These are read-path FINDING kinds. The sentinel's wire format has its own
frozen vocabulary — see [Signal kinds](/reference/signal-kinds/).

| Kind | Severity | Claim | Emitted by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `addon.degraded` | critical, warning | a kube-system add-on (dns, proxy, cni, csi, metrics, connectivity) is short of replicas; critical when none are available | [`bundle`](/reference/bundle/), [`health`](/reference/health/), [`scan`](/reference/scan/), [`triage delta`](/reference/triage-delta/) |
| `audit.default_sa_automount` | warning | the pod runs as the namespace's default ServiceAccount with its token automounted, and something in the pod can use it | [`audit hardening`](/reference/audit-hardening/), [`scan`](/reference/scan/) |
| `audit.exemption_expired` | warning | an exemption entry has lapsed: the findings it used to annotate are being reported unqualified again | [`audit exemptions`](/reference/audit-exemptions/), [`scan`](/reference/scan/) |
| `audit.exemption_expiring` | info | an exemption entry lapses within --within — renew it or let it go deliberately | [`audit exemptions`](/reference/audit-exemptions/), [`scan`](/reference/scan/) |
| `audit.host_namespace` | warning | the pod shares the node's network, PID, or IPC namespace | [`audit hardening`](/reference/audit-hardening/), [`scan`](/reference/scan/) |
| `audit.hostpath_mount` | warning, info | the pod mounts a host path; warning when it is writable, info when read-only | [`audit hardening`](/reference/audit-hardening/), [`scan`](/reference/scan/) |
| `audit.hpa_cannot_scale` | warning | the autoscaler structurally cannot scale: min equals max, the target is missing, or a container has no request for its utilization target to divide by | [`audit workloads`](/reference/audit-workloads/), [`scan`](/reference/scan/) |
| `audit.legacy_metadata` | warning | a node pool still serves the pre-v1 instance-metadata endpoints, which any pod can read | [`audit cluster`](/reference/audit-cluster/), [`scan`](/reference/scan/) |
| `audit.netpol_missing` | warning, info | nothing restricts this direction for the subject — a namespace with no policy at all, or a workload the covering policies' selectors miss; info for the egress direction, where no policy is a defensible default | [`audit netpol`](/reference/audit-netpol/), [`scan`](/reference/scan/) |
| `audit.no_liveness_probe` | info | a container has no liveness probe, so a wedged process is never restarted | [`audit workloads`](/reference/audit-workloads/), [`scan`](/reference/scan/) |
| `audit.no_pdb` | warning | the workload has no PodDisruptionBudget: a drain can take every replica at once | [`audit workloads`](/reference/audit-workloads/), [`scan`](/reference/scan/) |
| `audit.no_readiness_probe` | warning | a container has no readiness probe, so traffic reaches it before it can serve | [`audit workloads`](/reference/audit-workloads/), [`scan`](/reference/scan/) |
| `audit.no_spread` | info | the workload's replicas are not spread across nodes or zones | [`audit workloads`](/reference/audit-workloads/), [`scan`](/reference/scan/) |
| `audit.podsecurity_gaps` | warning | the namespace enforces no Pod Security Admission level, so none of the above is prevented | [`audit hardening`](/reference/audit-hardening/), [`scan`](/reference/scan/) |
| `audit.privileged_container` | warning | a container runs privileged or holds a node-root capability (ALL, SYS_ADMIN): a container escape is a node compromise | [`audit hardening`](/reference/audit-hardening/), [`scan`](/reference/scan/) |
| `audit.public_control_plane` | warning, info | the control-plane endpoint is reachable from the internet; info when authorized networks narrow it | [`audit cluster`](/reference/audit-cluster/), [`scan`](/reference/scan/) |
| `audit.rigid_scheduling` | warning, info | placement constraints pin the workload to too few nodes to survive losing one | [`audit workloads`](/reference/audit-workloads/), [`scan`](/reference/scan/) |
| `audit.single_replica` | warning | the workload runs a single replica, so any disruption is an outage | [`audit workloads`](/reference/audit-workloads/), [`scan`](/reference/scan/) |
| `audit.suspended_cronjob` | warning | a CronJob has been suspended past --cron-suspended and has skipped activations because of it: whatever it does is not happening, and nothing else reports that | [`audit workloads`](/reference/audit-workloads/), [`scan`](/reference/scan/) |
| `audit.upgrade_blocked` | warning, info | an active maintenance exclusion, or a node image on the removed Docker runtime, will stop the upgrade when it comes | [`audit upgrades`](/reference/audit-upgrades/), [`scan`](/reference/scan/) |
| `audit.upgrade_unattended` | info | upgrades will happen with nobody watching: no maintenance window, or no upgrade notifications | [`audit upgrades`](/reference/audit-upgrades/), [`scan`](/reference/scan/) |
| `audit.upgrade_unmanaged` | warning | nothing will close that gap on its own: no release channel, or node auto-upgrade/auto-repair off | [`audit upgrades`](/reference/audit-upgrades/), [`scan`](/reference/scan/) |
| `audit.version_behind` | warning, info | the control plane or a node pool is behind what the provider publishes, or a node pool has skewed from the control plane; info while the gap is still within the supported skew | [`audit upgrades`](/reference/audit-upgrades/), [`scan`](/reference/scan/) |

| `cert.invalid` | warning | a TLS secret's tls.crt does not contain a parseable X.509 certificate | [`health`](/reference/health/) |
| `change.config` | info | a ConfigMap in the neighborhood changed | [`triage changes`](/reference/triage-changes/) |

| `change.node` | info | a Node in the neighborhood changed | [`triage changes`](/reference/triage-changes/) |
| `change.rollout` | info | a workload's pod template changed — a new image, container or mount, or a controller churn event | [`triage changes`](/reference/triage-changes/) |
| `change.scale` | info | a workload's replica count changed | [`triage changes`](/reference/triage-changes/) |
| `change.secret` | info | a Secret in the neighborhood changed (names and shortened hashes only, never values —) | [`triage changes`](/reference/triage-changes/) |
| `change.topology` | info | a neighborhood object appeared, disappeared, or changed in a way none of the other classes name | [`triage changes`](/reference/triage-changes/) |
| `cloud.unavailable` | info | the cloud capability this check needs is unavailable, so nothing was examined — an explicit degradation record, never silence | [`audit cluster`](/reference/audit-cluster/), [`audit upgrades`](/reference/audit-upgrades/), [`cloud ipspace`](/reference/cloud-ipspace/), [`cloud orphans`](/reference/cloud-orphans/), [`cloud quota`](/reference/cloud-quota/), [`cloud stockout`](/reference/cloud-stockout/), [`perf probe`](/reference/perf-probe/), [`scan`](/reference/scan/), [`state wi`](/reference/state-wi/), [`triage top`](/reference/triage-top/) |

| `cron.unparseable` | warning | a CronJob's spec.schedule could not be parsed, so its activations cannot be judged at all | [`bundle`](/reference/bundle/), [`health`](/reference/health/), [`scan`](/reference/scan/), [`triage delta`](/reference/triage-delta/) |

The scorecard always answers, so healthy is explicit rather than silent; the line carries the worst severity found inside the category | [`health`](/reference/health/) |

| `storage.no_default_class` | critical | the claim names no class and the cluster has no default StorageClass | [`scan`](/reference/scan/), [`state storage`](/reference/state-storage/) |
| `storage.no_provisioner` | warning | the claim's class is static-only (kubernetes.io/no-provisioner) and no matching PV is available | [`scan`](/reference/scan/), [`state storage`](/reference/state-storage/) |
| `storage.pv_failed` | warning | a PersistentVolume is Failed: its reclaim did not complete, so the backing disk stays allocated and the volume cannot be reused | [`scan`](/reference/scan/), [`state storage`](/reference/state-storage/) |
| `storage.pv_released` | info | a PersistentVolume is Released — retained on purpose, but its capacity is unusable until spec.claimRef is cleared | [`scan`](/reference/scan/), [`state storage`](/reference/state-storage/) |
| `top.node` | critical, warning, info | a node's allocatable is close to committed — critical near the limit, info for an --all row below the threshold | [`triage top`](/reference/triage-top/) |
| `top.saturation` | critical, warning, info | a container's usage is close to its limit — critical near the limit, info for an --all row below the threshold | [`triage top`](/reference/triage-top/) |
| `top.unlimited` | info | how many containers in scope set no cpu/memory limit, and are therefore invisible to saturation analysis | [`triage top`](/reference/triage-top/) |
| `top.unlimited_container` | info | one container that sets no cpu/memory limit (--show-unlimited) | [`triage top`](/reference/triage-top/) |
| `top.unrequested` | info | how many containers in scope set no cpu/memory request, so the scheduler bin-packs them as zero | [`triage top`](/reference/triage-top/) |
| `top.unrequested_container` | info | one container that sets no cpu/memory request (--show-unrequested) | [`triage top`](/reference/triage-top/) |
| `triage.status` | info | the triage record for an incident subject as it now stands — state, root-cause hypothesis, action, and who wrote it; a receipt, not a defect | [`triage status`](/reference/triage-status/) |
| `volume.attach_error` | critical, warning | the attach or detach is failing; critical once it has been failing long enough to be stuck rather than slow | [`scan`](/reference/scan/), [`state volumes`](/reference/state-volumes/) |
| `volume.multi_attach` | critical | an RWO claim is wanted by pods on more than one node — the second pod never starts | [`scan`](/reference/scan/), [`state volumes`](/reference/state-volumes/) |
| `volume.orphaned_attachment` | info | a VolumeAttachment survives its PV or its node | [`scan`](/reference/scan/), [`state volumes`](/reference/state-volumes/) |
| `volume.zone_conflict` | critical | the PV is locked to a zone the pod's node is not in | [`scan`](/reference/scan/), [`state volumes`](/reference/state-volumes/) |
| `webhook.ca_expired` | critical | the webhook's caBundle has expired: the API server cannot verify it | [`health`](/reference/health/), [`scan`](/reference/scan/), [`state webhooks`](/reference/state-webhooks/) |
| `webhook.ca_expiring` | warning | the webhook's caBundle expires within --cert-warn | [`health`](/reference/health/), [`scan`](/reference/scan/), [`state webhooks`](/reference/state-webhooks/) |
| `webhook.dead_backend` | warning | the webhook's service backend is missing, has no ready endpoints, or does not serve the named port | [`health`](/reference/health/), [`scan`](/reference/scan/), [`state webhooks`](/reference/state-webhooks/) |
| `webhook.failing_closed` | critical | the webhook has no working backend and failurePolicy=Fail: every gated write is rejected cluster-wide | [`health`](/reference/health/), [`scan`](/reference/scan/), [`state webhooks`](/reference/state-webhooks/) |
| `webhook.slow_risk` | info | the webhook's timeout is long enough to slow every gated write if the backend degrades | [`health`](/reference/health/), [`scan`](/reference/scan/), [`state webhooks`](/reference/state-webhooks/) |
| `wi.gsa_missing` | critical | the annotated Google service account does not exist — every GCP call from these pods fails | [`scan`](/reference/scan/), [`state wi`](/reference/state-wi/) |
| `wi.unannotated_use` | info | a pod sets GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS but its ServiceAccount carries no Workload Identity annotation | [`scan`](/reference/scan/), [`state wi`](/reference/state-wi/) |
| `wi.unbound` | critical | the KSA annotates a GSA but the roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser binding is missing or malformed | [`scan`](/reference/scan/), [`state wi`](/reference/state-wi/) |
| `workload.replicafailure` | critical | the controller cannot create pods at all (quota, PodSecurity, admission) — no pod exists to diagnose | [`bundle`](/reference/bundle/), [`health`](/reference/health/), [`scan`](/reference/scan/), [`triage delta`](/reference/triage-delta/) |
| `workload.rollout` | critical, warning | replicas are short of desired; critical when nothing is serving at all | [`bundle`](/reference/bundle/), [`health`](/reference/health/), [`scan`](/reference/scan/), [`triage delta`](/reference/triage-delta/) |
| `workload.stalled` | critical | a Deployment's Progressing condition is False: the rollout has given up | [`bundle`](/reference/bundle/), [`health`](/reference/health/), [`scan`](/reference/scan/), [`triage delta`](/reference/triage-delta/) |
